history.summary: *** CSV DUPLICATE - CROSS-REFERENCE *** Seq 865 'Deshnoke Temple' is THE SAME TEMPLE as seq 861 'Karni Mata Temple'. Deshnoke (Deshnok) has one world-famous temple - the Karni Mata 'Temple of Rats' - and every source describing a 'Deshnoke Temple' in Bikaner district refers to it. There is no second, distinct 'Deshnoke Temple' with any web footprint. This file carries its own identity ('deshnoke-temple-karni-mata') only to hold the row; coordinator decision needed: MERGE this row into seq 861 or REMOVE one of the two rows to avoid double-counting. All substantive facts (history, deities, festivals, travel, timings) are documented in full under seq 861; what follows is a summary. The temple at Deshnoke, ~30 km south of Bikaner on NH62/NH89, is the celebrated rat temple: ~20,000-25,000 kabba rats are worshipped as reincarnated devotees of Karni Mata (the 14th-century Charan saint, 1387-1538, kuldevi of the Rathore houses of Bikaner and Jodhpur), with white rats treated as manifestations of the goddess herself. The domed inner sanctum dates to circa 1530 after her mahaprayana; Maharaja Ganga Singh rebuilt it in marble with solid-silver doors in the early 20th century. Open 4:00/4:30 AM-10:00 PM daily (verify); mangala aarti ~4:30 AM, sandhya aarti ~7 PM; free entry; remove shoes; no photos in the sanctum (verify).
